title: The Key to AI Software Security Isn’t Speed, It’s Maturity
description: This article discusses the security challenges posed by the adoption of agentic AI in software development. It highlights that rapid AI adoption without maturity and governance increases security risks, especially as AI agents become more autonomous. The piece outlines a three-phase, eight-stage AI Adoption Model that helps organizations understand their AI maturity and associated risks. It emphasizes the need for governance, developer upskilling, and observability to manage AI-driven security risks effectively. Most organizations are currently in early to mid-stages of AI adoption, making it critical to implement security controls and education programs now to prevent escalating risks as AI capabilities grow.
aiSummary: The article explains that the key to securing AI software development is maturity rather than speed. It presents a detailed AI Adoption Model with three phases—AI Assisted, AI Native, and Agentic—each with increasing levels of AI autonomy and associated risk. Early phases involve supervised AI assistance with low to moderate risk, while later phases involve unsupervised and fully autonomous AI agents with high to extreme risk levels. The article stresses that governance policies, developer training, and monitoring tools are essential to manage these risks. Without understanding their current AI adoption stage, organizations may fail to implement appropriate security measures, leading to vulnerabilities as AI agents perform more complex tasks autonomously.
aiImpact: The proliferation of agentic AI in software development expands the attack surface and increases security risks, with Gartner predicting a fourfold increase in incident costs related to agentic AI by 2027. AI models that generate code autonomously can introduce severe vulnerabilities if not properly governed. Organizations lacking visibility into AI usage and maturity risk falling behind in security controls, potentially leading to critical security incidents as AI agents operate with increasing autonomy.
